sentences.text:
3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
3.1.

It is the case of the appellants in this appeal are that at 7:00 am in the morning on 05-Mar-2007, deceased Thakor Kantiji Motiji, was while standing on the left hand road side of the sim of village Moti Hirwani, road to village Chacharia to Moti Hirwani, and while talking to the Mr. Prajapati Babubhai Kachrabhai and Mr. Thakor Pravinji Motiji was sitting pillion rider, on a scooter bearing registration no. GJ-2-P- 5163 owned and being drove by Mr. Prajapati Babubhai Kachrabhai had on way to Moti Hirwani from village Chacharia

, were in the sim of vil Moti Hirwani and on the correct side of the road, halted for talking, that, during one State Transport vehicle bearing registration no.GJ-18-V- 7143, being driven endangering human life with excessive speed, rashly and negligently coming from Moti Hirwani, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4484/2009 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined dashed with the scooter and the deceased and in the result, all three were succumbed to the serious injuries, died of vehicular accident because of sole negligence and rash driving of S.T.
Bus.
Hence, they have filed claim petition, which came to be dismissed.
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal has been preferred by claimants before this Court.
4. Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties.

5.1. Mr. Mayur Rajguru, learned advocate for the appellants has submitted that the Tribunal has committed gross error in holding the claimants themselves responsible for occurrence of the accident, and has also committed error in giving finding in negative on issue no.1 regarding the negligence of the respondent - S.T. Corporation.

Furthermore, he has submitted that the Tribunal has erred as the Tribunal has not assessed the income though there were sufficient material available on the record through the evidence of the parties, and pleadings of the parties.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4484/2009 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined 5.2.

Furthermore, he has submitted that the Tribunal has grossly erred in coming to the conclusion that the accident has occurred due to the fact that the deceased persons were coming in opposite direction of S.T. Corporation on scooter and three persons were sitting on scooter, and therefore,
S.T. Corporation cannot be held liable considering the deposition of the driver of the S.T.
Corporation Bus and also considering the Panchnama of the scene of offene.

Additionally, he has submitted that the Tribunal has grossly misread and miss-appreciated facts by wrongfully drawing conclusions against the deceased persons based on the deposition of the S.T. bus driver, who himself was the tort-feasor, and against whom a charge-sheet has been filed.
5.3. He has also pointed out that F.I.R. was also lodged by a third party, Arvindbhai Chaudhary, who was present at the time of the accident and who lodged the F.I.R. with the Police.

In the F.I.R.,

sentences.text: Arvindbhai stated that two of the deceased persons were on a scooter, and the third person met them on the side of the road.

While they were talking, the S.T. bus, traveling from NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4484/2009 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined Moti Hirwani to Chacharia,
hit and injured Thakor Kantiji Motiji, Prajapati Babubhai Kachrabhai, and Thakor Pravinji Motiji.
5.4. He has submitted that the said F.I.R. was not properly dealt with by the Tribunal while deciding the aspect of negligence.

The Tribunal has merely picked and chosen some part of evidence of the said witness, Arvindbhai Chaudhary, who was examined before the Tribunal as he has failed to narrate exact distance that from where he has seen the actual accident and, therefore, the Tribunal has not considered his deposition as germane.
Moreover, the Tribunal noted that Arvindbhai turned hostile in the Criminal Court, and therefore, his deposition should not be believed.
5.5. He has also drawn the attention to his detailed written statement and several judgments relevant to the present group of appeals.

He has relied on judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court, in the cases of (i) Smt.
Kaushnuma Begum And Ors. vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. reported in (2001) 2 SCC 9, (ii)
Janabhai vs. Ms. ICICI Lombard Insurance Company NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4484/2009 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined reported in 2022 (0) Supreme (SC) 706, (iii) Ravi Kapoor vs. State of Rajasthan reported in (2012) 9 SCC 284.

sentences.text: He has submitted that, according to the principle of res ipsa loquitur, whereby it is found that S.T. Bus is damaged from the front and ride side, and blood stains are also found.
Moreover, from the Panchnama, it is found that there are break marks found from 27 feet, which shows that the bus was moving in excessive speed.

Furthermore, he has submitted that considering the principle of "res ipsa loquitur", as F.I.R. is filed against the driver of S.T. Bus and charge-sheet is also filed against him, and also considering the fact that from the Panchnama, the scooter is found under the wheel of the S.T., But, the S.T. bus cannot be exonerated from the liability.

In fact, the Tribunal ought to have considered the negligence of S.T.
Bus, and ought to have found issue No.1 in affirmative by holding that S.T. bus remained negligent in causing accident.

Furthermore, he has submitted that even the Tribunal has failed to discharge its duty by even calculating the compensation though it might not have been awarded as the entire documentary as well as oral evidence is produced by the parties, and the Tribunal could certainly have assessed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4484/2009 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined the amount of compensation on the basis of same, which the Tribunal has failed to do so, and therefore,
he has submitted that he has prayed to allow the present appeal by granting the appropriate amount of compensation, and also by holding the respondent S.T. Corporation liable to pay the amount of compensation as the accident has occurred due to negligence of S.T. bus driver and, therefore, he has submitted that the impugned order passed by the Tribunal is required to be set aside.
5.6. He has further submitted that the Tribunal has failed in its duty by not calculating the compensation, even though the entire documentary and oral evidence was presented.
Thus, the Tribunal should have assessed the compensation amount, which it failed to do.

Therefore, he prayed to allow the present appeal by granting the appropriate amount of compensation and holding the respondent S.T. Corporation liable to pay it, as the accident occurred due to the negligence of the S.T. bus driver.
Consequently, he submitted that the impugned order passed by the Tribunal should be set aside.

sentences.text: Per contra, Mr. H.S. Munshaw, learned advocate for the respondent has drawn my attention to the witness, Arvindbhai and driver of S.T. Corporation; as well as the Panchnama of the place of accident.

He has also drawn attention of this Court towards the record and proceedings, along with paper-book, which are lying with this Court, and has submitted that the Tribunal has considered this aspect concluding that the said witnessed - Arvindbhai Chaudhary has failed to support the case of the claimants, and on the contrary, he has not stated the correct version of the incident and, therefore, the Tribunal has not believed his deposition.
The driver of the S.T. Bus, who can also be considered as eye-witness, has given the correct version that how the accident has occurred.

Furthermore, he has drawn the attention of this Court towards Panchnama of the scene of the accident, and has submitted that accident has occurred, whereby S.T. bus is found on the left side of the road, and the scooter is found the right side i.e. driver's side under the bus, as well as front part of the S.T. bus is also got damaged.
Furthermore, he has submitted that break mark shows that driver has driver has tried to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4484/2009 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined avoid the accident.
Furthermore, he has submitted that from the material available on the record, it clearly evident that S.T. bus is not negligent.

In fact, the case, which is pleaded by the claimants, is not believable that the deceased were standing at the side of road while chit-chatting, and at that point of time, S.T. bus came in rash and negligent manner and has caused the accident.
On the contrary, the facts are proved by the deposition of the driver as well as by the Panchnama, which supports each other.

Hence, there is no error committed by the Tribunal by finding that S.T. bus cannot be held liable,
and has prayed that appropriate order may be passed after considering the rival submissions of the parties.
8.1. I have considered the rival submissions of the respective parties.
I have gone through the record and proceedings.

It transpires that the Tribunal has failed it discharging its duty to assess the compensation, by holding that S.T. Corporation is not liable and only deceased are liable for occurring the accident, and due to that accident, they lost their life.

The Tribunal has committed error in concluding that deposition of eye- NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4484/2009 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined witness - Arvindbhai Chaudhary is not believable, and the deposition of driver of S.T. bus, who himself is one of the tort-feasor, is required to be believed.
The Tribunal seems to have committed in not properly appreciating the Panchnama of the site in question.
It transpires that the accident has occurred on the internal road, when S.T. bus is going from village Moti Hirwani to village Chacharia.

8.2. It transpires that at that time, eye-witness Arvindbhai was going on the same road, and he has seen the accident, whereby as per the F.I.R. lodged by him before the Police, whereby he has stated that when he was going on scooter, in from of his scooter, two persons were going on scooter, at that point of time, deceased Thakor Kantiji Motiji, who was standing on the side of the road, with the other two persons, who were going on scooter bearing registration No.2P 5163 were talking to each other standing on the side of the road.
At that point of time, S.T. bus bearing registration No.GJ-18-U-7143 has come in full speed and dashed with the scooter as well as three persons, who were standing on the side of the road.

The scooter was also dragging NEUTRAL CITATION Thakor Kantiji Motiji Since Decd. ... vs G S R T C on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129096121/

therefore, it transpires that there is some contradiction from the first version of F.I.R. as well as his deposition, but the fact remains that his has witnessed the accident, and he has lodged the F.I.R.
within few hours after the accident.

sentences.text: Moreover, the written statement filed by the S.T. Corporation does not disclose anything about the correctness of the accident, nor anything is stated that the driver of the S.T. Corporation is not negligent, and the accident is caused due to negligence of the deceased (scooter) and, therefore, such proof, which is tried to be given by examining the driver of S.T., is found without any pleading in the written statement.

Hence, the Tribunal has committed error in admitting the version given by the driver of the S.T. bus, as if it is gospels truth, which is totally erroneous, and is highly unwarranted, more particularly, when the driver of S.T. bus himself is found tort-feasor in the present accident, and as per version of claimants, the driver of S.T. bus has caused the accident, moreover, the charge-sheet is also filed against the driver of the S.T. bus,
and even Panchnama speaks about the accident, and there is no mention about the width of the road and, therefore, it NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4484/2009 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined cannot be said that accident has happened at which place, but from the break marks from about 27 feet to the S.T bus, it clearly indicates that S.T. bus was in excessive speed and, therefore, in all possibility, the accident might have occurred due to negligence of driver of S.T. bus, and the Tribunal has failed to consider all these aspects.
Additionally, the Tribunal has also failed to assess the income as required in the claim petition of the claimants.

8.3. Considering the fact that the present claim petition is of the year 2007, and the claimants have not received any amount till date, it is appropriate to remand back the matter by quashing and setting aside the amount judgment and order passed by the Tribunal to the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.) Mehsana to decide the present matters afresh, after giving proper opportunity of hearing to the parties by considering the materials available on the record and by considering the documentary as well as oral evidence on the record afresh and by giving cogent and convincing findings on all the issues, including issue of negligence.
Such exercise shall be carried out on or before 31.10.2024.
